status.en: 132 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 132 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen abducted six internally displaced persons on their way to farms in Kaduna and killed a farmer in Kaduna after receiving a N56 million ransom, while bandits killed a 3‑year-old girl in Zamfara after a kidnapping. Armed attackers assaulted Peter Obi opposition rallies and NDC supporters in Lagos, killing supporters and prompting a police probe. Troops ambushed and neutralised fourteen bandits in Katsina, and police rescued a kidnapped child in Zamfara. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn bortførte seks internt fordrevne på vei til gårder i Kaduna og drepte en bonde i Kaduna etter å ha mottatt en løsepenger på N56 millioner, mens banditter drepte en 3‑årig jente i Zamfara etter en kidnapping. Væpnede angripere angrep Peter Obi-opposisjonsrallier og NDC-tilhengere i Lagos, drepte tilhengere og førte til en politietterforskning. Tropper la en bakhold og nøytraliserte fjorten banditter i Katsina, og politiet reddet et bortført barn i Zamfara. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
